passages.text: In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of the Danites was looking for territory to occupy. For up to that time they had not come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
passages.sermon:
In those days, Israel had no king.
The people had no ruler.
The tribe of Dan was one of the tribes of Israel.
The tribe of Dan looked for land to live in.
They did not have their own land yet.
Until that day, the tribe of Dan had not received an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבַיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם שֵׁ֣בֶט הַדָּנִ֞י מְבַקֶּשׁ־ ל֤וֹ נַֽחֲלָה֙ לָשֶׁ֔בֶת כִּי֩ לֹֽא־ נָ֨פְלָה לּ֜וֹ עַד־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא בְּתוֹךְ־ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּנַחֲלָֽה׃ס

passages.text: So the Danites sent out five men from their clans, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. “Go and explore the land,” they told them. The men entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Dan had no land among the tribes of Israel.
The Danites wanted to find territory to live in.
The Danites chose five men from their clans.
These five men were brave warriors.
They came from Zorah and Eshtaol.
The Danites sent these men to spy out the land.
They told the men, “Go and explore the land.”
The five men traveled to the hill country of Ephraim.
They reached the house of Micah.
They stayed there for the night.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ בְנֵי־ דָ֣ן׀ מִֽמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּ֡ם חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֣ים מִקְצוֹתָם֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים בְּנֵי־ חַ֜יִל מִצָּרְעָ֣ה וּמֵֽאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֗ל לְרַגֵּ֤ל אֶת־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וּלְחָקְרָ֔הּ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לְכ֖וּ חִקְר֣וּ אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַר־ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ עַד־ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: And while they were near Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they went over and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”
passages.sermon:
The Danite men came near Micah’s house.
They heard a voice.
They recognized the voice.
The voice belonged to a young Levite.
They turned aside and went to him.
They spoke to the young Levite.
They asked him, “Who brought you here?”
They asked him, “What are you doing in this place?”
They asked him, “Why are you here?”
passages.original: הֵ֚מָּה עִם־ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה הִכִּ֔ירוּ אֶת־ ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר הַלֵּוִ֑י וַיָּס֣וּרוּ שָׁ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ מִֽי־ הֱבִיאֲךָ֣ הֲלֹ֔ם וּמָֽה־ אַתָּ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ה בָּזֶ֖ה וּמַה־ לְּךָ֥ פֹֽה׃

passages.text: “Micah has done this and that for me,” he replied, “and he has hired me to be his priest.”
passages.sermon:
A young Levite lived in Micah’s house.
Micah hired the Levite.
Micah made the Levite his priest.
The Levite said, “Micah did these things for me.”
The Levite said, “Micah hired me.”
The Levite said, “I became his priest.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כָּזֹ֣ה וְכָזֶ֔ה עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י מִיכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׂכְּרֵ֕נִי וָאֱהִי־ ל֖וֹ לְכֹהֵֽן׃

passages.text: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey.”
passages.sermon:
Five men from the tribe of Dan spoke to the young Levite.
The Levite lived in Micah’s house.
The men said to the Levite, “Ask God for us.”
They wanted to know if their journey would succeed.
They asked, “Will our journey be successful?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ שְׁאַל־ נָ֣א בֵאלֹהִ֑ים וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה הֲתַצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכֵּ֔נוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנַ֖חְנוּ הֹלְכִ֥ים עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: And the priest told them, “Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey.”
passages.sermon:
A priest spoke to the men.
He said, "Go in peace."
The LORD sees your journey.
The LORD watches over the way you will go.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לְכ֣וּ לְשָׁל֑וֹם נֹ֣כַח יְהוָ֔ה דַּרְכְּכֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּֽלְכוּ־ בָֽהּ׃פ

passages.text: So the five men departed and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living securely, like the Sidonians, tranquil and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking in the land and no oppressive ruler. And they were far away from the Sidonians and had no alliance with anyone.
passages.sermon:
Five men left their home.
They traveled to the city of Laish.
They saw the people who lived in Laish.
The people in Laish lived in safety.
They felt secure.
They lived peacefully, like the Sidonians.
The people were quiet and unsuspecting.
The land had everything they needed.
No one in the land oppressed them.
No ruler caused them trouble.
The people of Laish lived far from the Sidonians.
They had no alliance with any other people.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לָ֑יְשָׁה וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ יוֹשֶֽׁבֶת־ לָ֠בֶטַח כְּמִשְׁפַּ֨ט צִדֹנִ֜ים שֹׁקֵ֣ט׀ וּבֹטֵ֗חַ וְאֵין־ מַכְלִ֨ים דָּבָ֤ר בָּאָ֙רֶץ֙ יוֹרֵ֣שׁ עֶ֔צֶר וּרְחֹקִ֥ים הֵ֙מָּה֙ מִצִּ֣דֹנִ֔ים וְדָבָ֥ר אֵין־ לָהֶ֖ם עִם־ אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: When the men returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers asked them, “What did you find?”
passages.sermon:
Five men returned to their people.
They came back to Zorah and Eshtaol.
Their brothers saw them.
Their brothers spoke to them.
Their brothers asked a question.
They said, “What did you find?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־ אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם צָרְעָ֖ה וְאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם מָ֥ה אַתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: They answered, “Come on, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Why would you fail to act? Do not hesitate to go there and take possession of the land!
passages.sermon:
The five men spoke to their brothers from the tribe of Dan.
They said, “Get up.
Let us go attack the people of Laish.
We have seen the land.
The land is very good.
You are silent and doing nothing.
Do not be lazy.
Go and enter the land.
Take possession of it.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ ק֚וּמָה וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֤י רָאִ֙ינוּ֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה טוֹבָ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וְאַתֶּ֣ם מַחְשִׁ֔ים אַל־ תֵּעָ֣צְל֔וּ לָלֶ֥כֶת לָבֹ֖א לָרֶ֥שֶׁת אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: When you enter, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a spacious land, for God has delivered it into your hand. It is a place where nothing on earth is lacking.”
passages.sermon:
The Danite men spoke to their brothers.
They said, “When you enter the land, you will find a people who do not expect you.
These people feel safe.
The land is wide and open.
God has given this land into your hand.
This place has everything you need.
Nothing is missing in this land.”
passages.original: כְּבֹאֲכֶ֞ם תָּבֹ֣אוּ׀ אֶל־ עַ֣ם בֹּטֵ֗חַ וְהָאָ֙רֶץ֙ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדַ֔יִם כִּֽי־ נְתָנָ֥הּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם מָקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵֽין־ שָׁ֣ם מַחְס֔וֹר כָּל־ דָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: So six hundred Danites departed from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war.
passages.sermon:
Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan prepared for battle.
They came from the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol.
Each man carried weapons of war.
These men left their homes together.
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַדָּנִ֔י מִצָּרְעָ֖ה וּמֵאֶשְׁתָּאֹ֑ל שֵֽׁשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֔ישׁ חָג֖וּר כְּלֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim is called Mahaneh-dan to this day.
passages.sermon:
The Danite clan traveled up from their land.
They camped at Kiriath-jearim.
Kiriath-jearim is in Judah.
They named the place Mahaneh-dan.
Mahaneh-dan means "Camp of Dan."
This place is west of Kiriath-jearim.
People still call it Mahaneh-dan today.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲל֗וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בְּקִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִ֖ים בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה עַל־ כֵּ֡ן קָרְאוּ֩ לַמָּק֨וֹם הַה֜וּא מַחֲנֵה־ דָ֗ן עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הִנֵּ֕ה אַחֲרֵ֖י קִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִֽים׃

passages.text: And from there they traveled to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.
passages.sermon:
Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan left Zorah and Eshtaol.
They carried weapons for war.
They traveled from there to the hill country of Ephraim.
They arrived at the house of Micah.
passages.original: וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ מִשָּׁ֖ם הַר־ אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־ בֵּ֥ית מִיכָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their brothers, “Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol? Now think about what you should do.”
passages.sermon:
Five men had gone to spy out the land of Laish.
These five men spoke to their brothers.
They said, “Did you know something?”
They said, “These houses have special objects.”
They said, “There is an ephod here.”
They said, “There are household gods here.”
They said, “There is a graven image here.”
They said, “There is a molten idol here.”
They said, “Now, think about what you should do.”
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲנ֞וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַהֹלְכִים֮ לְרַגֵּל֮ אֶת־ הָאָ֣רֶץ לַיִשׁ֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־ אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם הַיְדַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣שׁ בַּבָּתִּ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ אֵפ֣וֹד וּתְרָפִ֔ים וּפֶ֖סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֖ה דְּע֥וּ מַֽה־ תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃

passages.text: So they turned aside there and went to the home of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and greeted him.
passages.sermon:
The men turned aside from their journey.
They went to the house of Micah.
A young Levite lived in Micah’s house.
The men greeted the young Levite.
passages.original: וַיָּס֣וּרוּ שָׁ֔מָּה וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ אֶל־ בֵּֽית־ הַנַּ֥עַר הַלֵּוִ֖י בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ־ ל֖וֹ לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: The six hundred Danites stood at the entrance of the gate, armed with their weapons of war.
passages.sermon: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan stood at the entrance of the gate.\r\nEach man wore his weapons for battle.\r\nThey were ready for war.
passages.original: וְשֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ חֲגוּרִים֙ כְּלֵ֣י מִלְחַמְתָּ֔ם נִצָּבִ֖ים פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִבְּנֵי־ דָֽן׃

passages.text: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred armed men.
passages.sermon:
Five men had gone to spy out the land.
These five men went inside Micah’s house.
They took the graven image.
They took the ephod.
They took the household idols.
They took the molten idol.
The priest stood at the entrance of the gate.
Six hundred men stood with the priest.
These six hundred men were armed for war.
These men were from the tribe of Dan.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲל֞וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַהֹלְכִים֮ לְרַגֵּ֣ל אֶת־ הָאָרֶץ֒ בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔מָּה לָקְח֗וּ אֶת־ הַפֶּ֙סֶל֙ וְאֶת־ הָ֣אֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת־ הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת־ הַמַּסֵּכָ֑ה וְהַכֹּהֵ֗ן נִצָּב֙ פֶּ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְשֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת הָאִ֔ישׁ הֶחָג֖וּר כְּלֵ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: When they entered Micah’s house and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
passages.sermon:
Five men entered Micah’s house.
They took the graven image.
They took the ephod.
They took the household idols.
They took the molten idol.
The priest saw them.
The priest spoke to them.
The priest said, “What are you doing?”
passages.original: וְאֵ֗לֶּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־ פֶּ֣סֶל הָאֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת־ הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת־ הַמַּסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן מָ֥ה אַתֶּ֖ם עֹשִֽׂים׃

passages.text: “Be quiet,” they told him. “Put your hand over your mouth and come with us and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?”
passages.sermon:
The five men from the tribe of Dan spoke to the priest.
They said, “Be quiet.”
They said, “Put your hand over your mouth.”
They said, “Come with us.”
They said, “Be a father to us.”
They said, “Be a priest to us.”
They asked, “Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one man?”
They asked, “Or is it better for you to be a priest for a tribe and a family in Israel?”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ ל֨וֹ הַחֲרֵ֜שׁ שִֽׂים־ יָדְךָ֤ עַל־ פִּ֙יךָ֙ וְלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֔נוּ וֶֽהְיֵה־ לָ֖נוּ לְאָ֣ב וּלְכֹהֵ֑ן הֲט֣וֹב׀ הֱיוֹתְךָ֣ כֹהֵ֗ן לְבֵית֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד א֚וֹ הֱיוֹתְךָ֣ כֹהֵ֔ן לְשֵׁ֥בֶט וּלְמִשְׁפָּחָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So the priest was glad and took the ephod, the household idols, and the graven image, and went with the people.
passages.sermon:
The priest was with Micah in his house.
The priest saw the men from the tribe of Dan.
The men from Dan told the priest to come with them.
The priest felt happy.
The priest took the ephod.
The priest took the household idols.
The priest took the graven image.
The priest went with the people from Dan.
passages.original: וַיִּיטַב֙ לֵ֣ב הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֵפ֔וֹד וְאֶת־ הַתְּרָפִ֖ים וְאֶת־ הַפָּ֑סֶל וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Putting their small children, their livestock, and their possessions in front of them, they turned and departed.
passages.sermon:
The Danites were a tribe in Israel.
They turned around.
They left the place.
They put their small children in front of them.
They put their livestock in front of them.
They put their possessions in front of them.
passages.original: וַיִּפְנ֖וּ וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ אֶת־ הַטַּ֧ף וְאֶת־ הַמִּקְנֶ֛ה וְאֶת־ הַכְּבוּדָּ֖ה לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: After they were some distance from Micah’s house, the men in the houses near Micah’s house mobilized and overtook the Danites.
passages.sermon:
The Danites left Micah’s house and traveled some distance away.
Men lived in houses near Micah’s house.
These men gathered together and raised an outcry.
They pursued the Danites.
They caught up with the Danites.
passages.original: הֵ֥מָּה הִרְחִ֖יקוּ מִבֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּבָּתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עִם־ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה נִֽזְעֲק֔וּ וַיַּדְבִּ֖יקוּ אֶת־ בְּנֵי־ דָֽן׃

passages.text: When they called out after them, the Danites turned to face them and said to Micah, “What is the matter with you that you have called out such a company?”
passages.sermon:
The men near Micah’s house called out after the Danites.
The Danites heard the call.
The Danites turned to face the men.
The Danites spoke to Micah.
The Danites asked Micah a question.
They said, “What is the matter with you?”
They said, “Why have you called out such a company?”
passages.original: וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵי־ דָ֔ן וַיַּסֵּ֖בּוּ פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְמִיכָ֔ה מַה־ לְּךָ֖ כִּ֥י נִזְעָֽקְתָּ׃

passages.text: He replied, “You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’ ”
passages.sermon:
Micah was a man who lived near the tribe of Dan.
Micah had made idols for himself.
Micah also had a priest who served him.
The Danites took Micah’s idols.
The Danites took Micah’s priest.
The Danites left with them.
Micah spoke to the Danites.
Micah said, “You took the gods I made.
You took my priest.
You went away with them.
I have nothing left.
Why do you ask me, ‘What is the matter with you?’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר אֶת־ אֱלֹהַי֩ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֨יתִי לְקַחְתֶּ֧ם וְֽאֶת־ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן וַתֵּלְכ֖וּ וּמַה־ לִּ֣י ע֑וֹד וּמַה־ זֶּ֛ה תֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלַ֖י מַה־ לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: The Danites said to him, “Do not raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”
passages.sermon:
The Danites were a tribe of Israel.
The Danites spoke to Micah.
They said, "Do not let your voice be heard among us."
They warned Micah not to speak loudly to them.
They said, "If you do, angry men may attack you."
They said, "You may lose your life."
They said, "Your family may also lose their lives."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ בְּנֵי־ דָ֔ן אַל־ תַּשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלְךָ֖ עִמָּ֑נוּ פֶּֽן־ יִפְגְּע֣וּ בָכֶ֗ם אֲנָשִׁים֙ מָ֣רֵי נֶ֔פֶשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ֥ה נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: So the Danites went on their way, and Micah turned to go back home, because he saw that they were too strong for him.
passages.sermon:
The Danites were a tribe of Israel.
The Danites took Micah’s idols and his priest.
The Danites left and continued on their way.
Micah saw the Danites were stronger than he was.
Micah turned around.
Micah went back to his home.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ בְנֵי־ דָ֖ן לְדַרְכָּ֑ם וַיַּ֣רְא מִיכָ֗ה כִּי־ חֲזָקִ֥ים הֵ֙מָּה֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וַיִּ֖פֶן וַיָּ֥שָׁב אֶל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: After they had taken Micah’s idols and his priest, they went to Laish, to a tranquil and unsuspecting people, and they struck them with their swords and burned down the city.
passages.sermon:
The Danites took the idols that Micah had made.
They also took the priest who belonged to Micah.
The Danites went to the city of Laish.
The people of Laish were peaceful and unsuspecting.
The Danites attacked the people of Laish with their swords.
They killed the people of Laish.
The Danites burned the city of Laish with fire.
passages.original: וְהֵ֨מָּה לָקְח֜וּ אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֣ה מִיכָ֗ה וְֽאֶת־ הַכֹּהֵן֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָה־ לוֹ֒ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַל־ לַ֗יִשׁ עַל־ עַם֙ שֹׁקֵ֣ט וּבֹטֵ֔חַ וַיַּכּ֥וּ אוֹתָ֖ם לְפִי־ חָ֑רֶב וְאֶת־ הָעִ֖יר שָׂרְפ֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: There was no one to deliver them, because the city was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone; it was in a valley near Beth-rehob. And the Danites rebuilt the city and lived there.
passages.sermon:
The people of Laish had no one to save them.
Their city was far from Sidon.
They had no alliance with any other people.
Their city was in a valley near Beth-rehob.
The Danites rebuilt the city.
The Danites lived in the city.
passages.original: וְאֵ֨ין מַצִּ֜יל כִּ֧י רְֽחוֹקָה־ הִ֣יא מִצִּיד֗וֹן וְדָבָ֤ר אֵין־ לָהֶם֙ עִם־ אָדָ֔ם וְהִ֕יא בָּעֵ֖מֶק אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְבֵית־ רְח֑וֹב וַיִּבְנ֥וּ אֶת־ הָעִ֖יר וַיֵּ֥שְׁבוּ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: They named it Dan, after their forefather Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city was formerly named Laish.
passages.sermon:
The Danites took over the city of Laish.
They changed the name of the city.
They called the city Dan.
They named it after their ancestor Dan.
Dan was a son of Israel.
Before this, the city was called Laish.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ שֵׁם־ הָעִיר֙ דָּ֔ן בְּשֵׁם֙ דָּ֣ן אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוּלַּ֖ד לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאוּלָ֛ם לַ֥יִשׁ שֵׁם־ הָעִ֖יר לָרִאשֹׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: The Danites set up idols for themselves, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Dan set up an idol for themselves.
Jonathan was the son of Gershom.
Gershom was the son of Moses.
Jonathan and his sons served as priests for the tribe of Dan.
They served as priests until the land was taken captive.
passages.original: וַיָּקִ֧ימוּ לָהֶ֛ם בְּנֵי־ דָ֖ן אֶת־ הַפָּ֑סֶל וִ֠יהוֹנָתָן בֶּן־ גֵּרְשֹׁ֨ם בֶּן־ מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה ה֣וּא וּבָנָ֗יו הָי֤וּ כֹהֲנִים֙ לְשֵׁ֣בֶט הַדָּנִ֔י עַד־ י֖וֹם גְּל֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: So they set up for themselves Micah’s graven image, and it was there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh.
passages.sermon:
The people of Dan set up Micah’s idol for themselves.
Micah had made this idol.
The idol remained with them.
It stayed there as long as the house of God was in Shiloh.
passages.original: וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ לָהֶ֔ם אֶת־ פֶּ֥סֶל מִיכָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה כָּל־ יְמֵ֛י הֱי֥וֹת בֵּית־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּשִׁלֹֽה׃פ
